influences.name: Lole y Manuel
influences.reason: Rosalía's 2017 album Los Ángeles was made in the spirit of these nuevo flamenco artists, establishing a foundational influence on her flamenco interpretation.

influences.name: James Blake
influences.reason: His synths and atmospherics inspired Rosalía's approach on tracks like 'PIENSO EN TU MIRÁ,' which combines R&B with flamenco vocal elements.

influences.name: Kendrick Lamar
influences.reason: Featured on Rosalía's influences playlist, contributing to her hip-hop and urbano musical direction.

influences.name: David Bowie
influences.reason: Rosalía's parents introduced her to Bowie's music, and he remains a key influence on her genre-bending approach.

influences.name: John Coltrane
influences.reason: Listed among Rosalía's key influences on her official influences playlist, contributing to her sophisticated musical palette.

influences.name: Camarón de la Isla
influences.reason: A foundational flamenco artist whose work directly inspired Rosalía's flamenco vocal technique and interpretation.

influences.name: La Niña de los Peines
influences.reason: Classic flamenco artist cited as a direct influence on Rosalía's flamenco-rooted artistic development.

influences.name: Kate Bush
influences.reason: Rosalía has explicitly cited Bush as an influence on her genre-bending, experimental approach to music.

influences.name: Lauryn Hill
influences.reason: An expressed influence on Rosalía's musical style, contributing to her R&B and urban music integration.

influences.name: Missy Elliott
influences.reason: Cited as an influence on Rosalía's innovative approach to hip-hop and electronic music production.

influences.name: Björk
influences.reason: An influential artist on Rosalía's experimental and boundary-pushing musical approach.

influences.name: Antonio Vivaldi
influences.reason: Classical composer whose work influenced Rosalía's later integration of classical elements, particularly evident in her LUX album.

influences.name: Nick Cave
influences.reason: Cited as an influence on Rosalía's dark, artistic sensibility and songwriting approach.

influences.name: Travis Scott
influences.reason: Hip-hop/trap producer who influenced Rosalía's urbano and electronic production style.

influences.name: Lola Flores
influences.reason: Spanish flamenco and performance artist cited as a direct influence on Rosalía's flamenco artistry.

influences.name: Justin Timberlake
influences.reason: His song 'Cry Me a River' was sampled on 'Bagdad' from El Mal Querer, representing his influence on Rosalía's production choices.

influences.name: Destiny's Child
influences.reason: Rosalía has woven their influence into her lyrics and musical approach, particularly regarding harmony and vocal arrangement.

influences.name: Arthur Russell
influences.reason: Rosalía has alluded to his work in her songwriting, influencing her eclectic fusion approach.

influences.name: Miguel Poveda
influences.reason: A flamenco artist with whom Rosalía collaborated early in her career, directly shaping her flamenco development.

influences.name: Juan Gómez "Chicuelo"
influences.reason: Flamenco guitarist and collaborator who influenced Rosalía's understanding of traditional flamenco music and guitar.

influences.name: Rocío Márquez
influences.reason: Spanish flamenco singer with whom Rosalía collaborated, contributing to her flamenco vocal training and style.

influences.name: La Paquera de Jerez
influences.reason: Her bulería was sampled on 'Que No Salga La Luna' from El Mal Querer, representing direct musical influence.

influences.name: Supertramp
influences.reason: Part of Rosalía's early musical exposure through her parents, influencing her eclectic taste and genre openness.

influences.name: Queen
influences.reason: Part of Rosalía's early musical exposure through her parents, contributing to her understanding of ambitious, genre-spanning music.

influences.name: Raül Refree
influences.reason: Spanish musician, composer, and record producer who co-produced Rosalía's debut album Los Ángeles and shaped her nuevo flamenco approach.
